🇺🇸🇮🇷 Even America’s biggest nuclear warhead probably can’t reach Iran’s Pickaxe Mountain, and firing one would hand Tehran the bomb it doesn’t yet have

Steven Starr, who studies nuclear weapons effects for the Los Alamos Study Group, ran the numbers with MIT’s Ted Postol.

The largest conventional bomb carries 11 tons of explosive. A tactical nuke at 50 kilotons digs maybe 30 meters into granite.

The 475-kiloton warhead on a Trident missile makes a crater about 100 meters deep... and the tunnels near Natanz sit between 260 and 600 meters down, behind concrete Iran says is 10 times stronger than normal.

“It really is a fool’s errand to try to go after this with a nuclear weapon.”

Steven says Iran already holds enough 60% uranium for 10 to 12 weapons, and that first mushroom cloud would decide the doctrine debate underway in Tehran right now, which is why officials reportedly split today between more strikes and a deal.
